scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows disputed bills are more frequent for actual reads (1,785) than for estimated reads (1,240), indicating that disputes are not driven primarily by estimation errors; other factors affecting actual‑read bills contribute significantly to the dispute surge.
The tariff change log shows no tariff changes recorded, indicating that tariff alterations are not a contributing factor to the recent dispute surge.
The observation shows dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3‑day SLA) with 2,440 tickets, indicating the surge is not due to delayed responses.
The observation shows dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 per month pre‑August to >1,100 in August and >1,200 in September, confirming a sustained doubling and upward trend.
The route completion for August‑September 2026 is 0.88, below the target of 0.95, indicating that manual meter read collection is falling short and may contribute to missing reads.
